strategy: Individual original native GLSL reconstructions, with bounded native numeric state where required; no JavaScript runtime or WebView. Source presence, candidate tests, deployment and hardware validation are separate. No claim of pixel identity.
scope_policy: Standard effects including screen, audio and keyboard interaction; no game integrations or specialized external APIs; personal sources only if title or filename contains free. Hidden records remain to be classified.

summary.counting_note: Distinct native presets:26 deployed and one additional Pump Up Beats candidate. Optical/input tests and exact rendering parity remain separate; most of the catalogue is not yet ported.

status_definitions.deployed_native_reconstruction: Reference-matched source and tested native implementation are deployed. No pixel identity or individual hardware validation is implied.
status_definitions.candidate_tested_pending_deployment: Reference-matched source, build, production GPU and native UI checks passed; not included in the deployed plugin.
status_definitions.not_ported: No implementation of this specific source record is supplied. Similar titles or control schemas do not confer support.
status_definitions.source_unavailable: Local reference source unavailable; algorithm and controls cannot be confirmed.

effects.title: Rainbow Pulse
effects.differences: The reference uses a 50 Hz hue advance and global white flash, including its initial fade from half white. Native keyboard events or preview taps reset a global flash; taps do not create spatial rings. Pulse-intensity edits affect a currently decaying flash immediately; the reference samples that setting at the hit. No claim of physical keyboard identity validation is made by this preset.

effects.title: Terminal
effects.differences: Original GPU reconstruction: 50 Hz glyph changes, one column per font-size unit, and 0.85-per-tick fading over 64 historical ticks. Hand-drawn 5×7 letters replace the browser font; deterministic bounded walks replace independent random motion. Color changes recolor the reconstructed trails; size changes rebuild them immediately. No keyboard input, font asset or proprietary effect code is included.

effects.title: Color Shift
effects.differences: A bounded native 60 Hz simulation preserves spawn countdown across speed edits, at most ten composited layers, alpha accumulation, zero-speed fade freeze and live HSL saturation/lightness. Random colors are deterministic original pseudorandom values, not the reference random sequence.

effects.title: Spiral Rainbow
effects.differences: Analytic sectors replace Canvas2D overlap and antialiasing. Reverse changes may reposition phase; elapsed-time speed matches the source.

effects.title: Space
effects.differences: Original GPU implementation, not redistributed Canvas source. Preserves the seven controls and layered-cloud/outward-star composition. Stable procedural seeds replace JavaScript randomness; star lifetimes and cloud oscillations use integrated animation speed at a normalized 60 Hz reference. Cloud speed response is continuous and linear instead of the original wall-clock-dependent curve. A zero animation speed freezes motion while live color/size controls remain usable. Particle placement, startup population and antialiasing differ; pixel identity is not claimed.

effects.title: Aurora
effects.differences: Original GPU implementation with the original six controls. Seeded curtains and smooth vertical wandering replace random per-frame movement. Analytic trails approximate the original persistent Canvas accumulation without storing past frames. Density zero clears curtains immediately instead of waiting for existing streaks to leave. Integrated speed preserves phase when speed changes; cycle changes recolor existing curtains immediately. Pixel identity and identical random particle histories are not claimed.

effects.title: Custom Spiral
effects.differences: Reference animation is calibrated at 60 Hz. Analytic sector edges replace overlapping Canvas2D wedges; reverse changes may reposition phase.

effects.title: Color Cycle
effects.differences: Speed is integrated continuously and normalized to the reference at 60 Hz. Zero freezes hue. The tiny one-degree reset discontinuity of the reference is replaced by a continuous hue wrap.

effects.title: Underwater
effects.differences: Original bounded GPU reconstruction with the original nine controls. Shimmers use a seeded spatial population, analytic trails and phase-based renewal rather than the source Canvas particle/history buffers. Fade retention is bounded, including at 100, and automatic ripples are capped at 32 simultaneous rings. Ripple Frequency changes their density and resulting event rate, approximating the original behavior at the default speed; it is not an exact spawn scheduler at other speeds. The latest native preview tap is supported through iTap; spatial keyboard events and multiple simultaneous tap histories are not ported. Pixel identity is not claimed.

effects.title: Gradient
effects.differences: RGB interpolation follows sorted stops including coincident stops. Identical endpoints render black; no previous Canvas2D frame is retained.

effects.title: Rainbow Rise
effects.differences: Reference animation is calibrated at 60 Hz. Continuous radial color replaces individual accumulated one-pixel Canvas2D strokes. Reverse changes may reposition phase.

effects.title: Custom Sunrise
effects.differences: Original analytic radial reconstruction with all seven controls, integrated radial speed, three-color sequence and reference 400-pixel radius. This is not pixel-perfect: it models dense bands rather than the finite 400-ring array, so its startup overlap, sparse-ring recycling and historical band colors after Scale edits differ. Scale edits reshape existing bands immediately; the reference retains each ring birth color. No original source or assets are embedded.

effects.scope_reason: Depends on Binance market data APIs.

effects.title: Police Lights
effects.differences: Native fixed-step 60 Hz timing preserves the rounded speed steps, the 0 through 4 speed dead zone, center flash, side swap and strict timing boundaries. No browser or script runtime.

effects.title: TV Static
effects.differences: Original deterministic per-cell noise changes at a nominal 60 Hz. Preserves pixel sizes, the 0/2/3 custom-color options, equal custom-palette selection and the rounded white-pixel draw distribution. Noise samples differ from browser randomness.

effects.title: Good Night!
effects.differences: Intentional all-black image, not an operating-system power command. Whether a physical device switches off for black remains its native driver policy.

effects.title: Quad-Color Breath
effects.differences: Native fixed-step 60 Hz state preserves tint limits, rotation at the dark end, the historical four-color order, and independent per-quadrant breathing flags. Turning rotation off reloads the chosen colors; turning it back on retains that palette until the next dark-end rotation. Timing is normalized to 60 Hz rather than browser frame rate.

effects.title: Crooked Waves
effects.differences: Native fixed-step 60 Hz state retains four bounded stripe positions, shared random color on wrap and resets positions when Bar Amount changes. Shader applies the 45-degree stripe transform and antialiasing. Random samples differ; the source initial blank/undefined-color frame is replaced by the selected color. Its commented-out Vertical control is not added.

effects.title: Gradient Wave
effects.differences: Reference animation is calibrated at 60 Hz. Frame-count wrap overshoot and HSL rounding are removed. Changing direction, wave size or color count immediately recomposes the field. Hue-cycle phase follows its integrated clock while disabled.

effects.title: Rainbow Tunnel
effects.differences: Reference geometry uses 50 rings in a 320x200 canvas and 60 Hz timing. Ring size changes radius spacing; stroke width stays 30 reference pixels. The original retained old strokes between frames; this stateless GPU port shows only current rings and cannot reproduce those historical trails.

effects.title: Neon Nebula
effects.differences: Original GLSL implementation; no redistributed Canvas source. Preserves all eight controls, three waves and their phase-dependent palette, persistent source-over accumulation, six-color square/ring population, initial teal and expanding color2 tap rings. Native ping-pong feedback never samples the texture being rendered. A fixed 300-particle seeded population replaces random births and the transient 30 growing startup squares; particle radii use their mature sizes. Animation and tap expansion use integrated speed at a normalized 60 Hz reference, while opacity accumulates once per rendered frame. Frame rate, random placement, startup population and antialiasing therefore affect pixel-level results. History clears on restart, resize and shader recompilation. Tap force controls ring opacity; speed changes do not jump an existing ring. No BPM or synthetic keypress is generated.

effects.title: Rainbow Tap
effects.hardware_validation: KBHE physical keys A/Q/Z/W/!/*/< correct, no duplicate triggers; user confirmed2026-09-27
effects.differences: Original GPU reconstruction; no original source code or assets are embedded. Preserves the five controls, overlapping ring order, stable random color per event and custom color updates. The source's 300-frame lifetime is normalized to five seconds at 60 Hz, with a final 0.75-second fade. Speed is integrated independently for each ring, so zero stops expansion but not expiry, and speed changes do not jump its radius. At most 64 live events are retained; oldest events are evicted if full. Antialiasing, randomness and timing at other reference frame rates differ. Keyboard locations require the native input mapping capability; preview taps use the same spatial contract.

effects.title: Galaxies
effects.differences: Original GPU reconstruction; no original implementation or assets are embedded. Retains all eight controls, their labels (including Vertical Postion), five named formations and the independent star field. Position controls set the rotation/scale pivot as in the reference, not an independent galaxy translation. Stable procedural seeds, continuously populated clouds and integrated phases replace random birth schedules and Canvas history. Expanding-arm populations are capped at 100, and analytic radial gradients approximate the reference gradients. All motion, including core pulsation, freezes at zero animation speed. Particle placement, startup, exact spiral growth and gradient interpolation differ; pixel identity is not claimed.

effects.title: Neon Shift
effects.differences: Uses native framebuffer feedback: five percent of each new frame approaches the next HSL target. This preserves frame-dependent blending; convergence therefore depends on selected render FPS. Integrated phase preserves speed changes and zero holds the current target while its blend continues. Reference palette colors and full saturation/halved lightness are retained.

effects.title: Rainbow
effects.differences: Reference animation is calibrated at 60 Hz. Smooth analytic sampling replaces the original 320x200 strips; controls remain in reference units.

effects.title: Side to Side
effects.differences: Reference animation is calibrated at 60 Hz. Rainbow hue selection is deterministic per sweep rather than Math.random. Frame overshoot at sweep completion is removed; direction changes restart geometry at the current integrated travel phase.

effects.title: Solid Color
effects.differences: Reference breathing is calibrated at 60 Hz. Direct RGB alpha multiplication avoids source HSL rounding. The integrated breathing clock continues while the toggle is off.
